sentences.text: 2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and the learned AGA.
However, none is present for the opposite party no.2 despite service of notice.
3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that in the said case the applicant is accused and the trial is at the stage of recording the evidence of prosecution witnesses.

The learned Presiding Officer uses to interfere with the evidence recorded before the Court and tries to cross-examine the witness himself, which was not expected from a Presiding Officer and hence the applicant has no hope of justice from the said Court.

The transfer application moved by the Kamlesh Joshi vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57351452/
1 applicant before the Sessions Judge, Chitrakoot has been rejected illegally without any cogent reason.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that in these facts and circumstances the applicant has moved the present transfer application before this Court.

4. Learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer and submitted that there is no substance in the allegations made in the transfer application against the Presiding Officer of the Court concerned and the transfer application is liable to be rejected.
5. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record carefully.

6. From a perusal of the allegations levelled against the Presiding Officer of the Court concerned it appears that the applicant, who is an accused in this case, wants to find out a Court of his own choice.
This is the duty of the Presiding Officer to remain active and cautious at the time of recording the evidence of witnesses before the Court.

He is expected not to be a mere spectator while the evidence is recorded before the Court and he may interrupt during the evidence, if it appears to him that the evidence is not being recorded in proper manner or the witness is unable to understand the questions offered to him or in any requisite circumstance.

Section 165 Evidence Act empowers the Court to put any question to any witness about any fact relevant or irrelevant and neither the parties nor their agents shall be entitled to make any objection to any such question or order nor without the leave of the Court, to cross-examine any witness upon any answer given in reply to any question.
Hence, in my opinion it is not a fit case to direct transfer of the aforesaid Session Trial to any other competent court.
The present transfer application being misconceived and baseless is rejected.
